strategies.title: [robust-local-regression] Robust LOWESS trend reconstruction
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: robust-local-regression

Replacement scope: Replace the complete `try` block in `enhanced_filter_with_trend_preservation`, including both `UnivariateSpline` fits, residual winsorization, and candidate selection. Preserve the existing finite-value repair and final `selected[window_size-1:]` slicing.

Compute budget: No optimizer. Use one deterministic robust LOWESS/LOESS pass over the full record with span `frac = clip(1.6*window_size/n, 0.035, 0.12)`, tricube distance weights, and exactly two bisquare residual-reweighting iterations. A vectorized implementation may use `statsmodels.nonparametric.smoothers_lowess.lowess`; otherwise use bounded overlapping windows with at most `ceil(n/4)` local fits. Expected evaluation-time effect is below 5x the current spline path and remains comfortably below the timeout for the supplied record sizes.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent's cubic smoothing spline distributes curvature globally and can create small oscillatory slope reversals near high-frequency components and repaired impulses. LOWESS replaces that global basis with compact, robust, locally weighted linear estimates: broad trends are smoothed, while genuine turning points are not forced to satisfy one global cubic curvature model. Use `it=2`, `delta=0`, and extrapolate the first and last local estimates by their local fitted slopes before slicing. Reject nonfinite results only by falling back to the incumbent spline output. The output remains exactly `n-window_size+1`.

Expected-gain check: this is a falsifiable local refinement if the produced aligned series reduces raw reversals from 22 to at most 19 while keeping aligned MAE no more than 0.3521, which would strictly improve the incumbent's reversal-dominated composite and combined ranking.

strategies.title: [switching-trend-hmm] Two-regime slope-state reconstruction
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: switching-trend-hmm

Replacement scope: Replace only the spline-and-winsorization phase after `repaired` is created. Keep the existing impulse repair, finite handling, and output-length slicing.

Compute budget: No numerical optimizer and no random starts. Construct a deterministic two-regime hidden Markov model whose observations are first differences of `repaired`: a low-variance “stationary/noise” regime and a high-variance “moving-trend” regime. Estimate both variances from the 25th and 75th percentiles of `abs(diff(repaired))`, use fixed transition persistence `0.94`, and perform exactly one forward-backward pass followed by one Viterbi pass. Expected evaluation-time effect is linear in `n` and negligible relative to the current spline call.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent smooths amplitudes but has no explicit persistence constraint on directional state. The HMM introduces a discrete slope topology: isolated sign changes remain in the noise regime and are suppressed, whereas runs of similarly signed increments remain in the moving regime and are reconstructed using their regime-weighted local slope. Reconstruct the level by integrating the posterior-weighted slope, anchor its additive constant to the robust median residual, and blend 20% of the repaired signal back into the reconstruction to limit lag. Use a three-sample minimum-duration rule on Viterbi moving states so one-sample noise excursions cannot create reversals. If the model degenerates, return the incumbent spline result. The final array is sliced exactly as before.

Expected-gain check: the new state-persistence topology is absent from the spline and cannot be represented by merely changing its smoothing factor; it should be accepted only if evaluator output has `slope_changes <= 18` and `lag_error <= 0.33`, a directly falsifiable threshold that would improve the current 22-reversal/0.313-lag tradeoff through the 30% reversal and 20% smoothness terms without materially sacrificing responsiveness.

strategies.title: [adaptive-kernel-mixture] Convex adaptive kernel mixture
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: adaptive-kernel-mixture

Replacement scope: Replace `enhanced_filter_with_trend_preservation` after finite-value repair with a full-record mixture of three fixed linear estimators: Gaussian kernels with standard deviations `0.8`, `1.6`, and `3.0` samples. Do not retain the spline phase or its reversal-count candidate selector.

Compute budget: No optimizer. Compute the three reflect-padded convolutions once, then calculate a local roughness score from a five-sample median absolute deviation of first differences. Map that score deterministically to softmax weights favoring the narrow kernel in rough/high-curvature regions and the broad kernel in quiet regions; use the medium kernel as the baseline with weight at least `0.25`. Expected evaluation-time effect is approximately three convolutions and one vectorized weight calculation, typically faster than the current spline path.

Gain mechanism: A single global spline smoothing factor cannot simultaneously preserve the signal's rapid sinusoidal curvature and suppress quiet-region noise. The mixture adds spatially varying bandwidth as a new degree of freedom: it prevents broad smoothing from flattening genuine changes while suppressing reversals in locally quiet regions. Smooth the weights with a three-sample moving average before blending so the bandwidth transition itself cannot create slope discontinuities. Apply the existing repaired samples only as a 10% residual correction, clipped to `±2.5` robust difference scales. Return exactly `mixture[window_size-1:]`; use the existing Gaussian fallback if any operation is nonfinite.

Expected-gain check: the construction can be evaluated against the explicit threshold `slope_changes <= 20`, `false_reversals <= 13`, and `avg_error <= 0.36`; satisfying all three would strictly improve the incumbent's 22 reversals, 14.4 false reversals, and 0.3521 average error, while preserving the hard output-length contract.

strategies.title: [robust-frequency-tilt] Robust spectral tilt with endpoint-preserving reconstruc
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: robust spectral-tilt reconstruction

Replacement scope: Replace the complete `try` block in `enhanced_filter_with_trend_preservation`, including spline fitting, residual winsorization, candidate selection, and exception fallback. Preserve the existing preprocessing and final `selected[window_size-1:]` contract.

Compute budget: No optimizer and no iterative solver; use one FFT-based transform, one inverse transform, and at most two vectorized robust-weighting passes. Expected runtime remains below 0.02 seconds for the supplied 1000-sample records.

Gain mechanism: Estimate the noise floor from the upper quartile of the periodogram, then apply a continuous Tukey spectral taper rather than a hard low-pass cutoff. Retain all bins below a data-derived transition frequency, smoothly attenuate bins in the transition band, and strongly suppress only bins whose power is consistent with broadband noise. Before transforming, replace isolated impulses using the existing robust difference scale. After inverse transformation, restore the low-frequency affine component by matching the robust least-squares level and slope of the repaired input; this prevents the spectral attenuation from flattening slow random-walk drift. Use reflection padding to at least three filter lengths before the FFT and crop back to the original record, then return the required suffix.

The construction adds frequency-selective attenuation and explicit low-frequency slope restoration, degrees of freedom unavailable to the incumbent's spline residual gate. It should reduce counted reversals caused by high-frequency noise while preserving the multi-frequency signal better than a single smoothing factor. Reject this idea if the implementation does not reduce the returned reversal count by at least 2 while increasing aligned mean absolute error by no more than 0.015 on the default generated record; that is a directly falsifiable evaluator threshold. Expected-gain check: the incumbent has 22 slope changes and 14.4 false reversals, so a reduction of at least two slope changes and one false reversal lowers both dominant reversal terms, and the thresholded error increase is smaller than the resulting composite improvement.

strategies.title: [robust-quantile-envelope] Quantile-envelope projection with curvature-limited b
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: robust quantile-envelope projection

Replacement scope: Replace only the `selected` construction and the final output extraction in `enhanced_filter_with_trend_preservation`; retain finite-value handling, impulse repair, and the spline `z` as the initial smooth proposal.

Compute budget: No optimizer; perform two sliding-window quantile evaluations, one vectorized clipping operation, and one curvature-limited blend. Use odd envelope width `max(5, 2*(window_size//4)+1)`. Expected evaluation time increases by less than 0.01 seconds per call.

strategies.title: [frequency-selective harmonic tracking] Deterministic harmonic state reconstruct
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: frequency-selective harmonic state tracking

Replacement scope: Replace the `UnivariateSpline` reconstruction and residual-gating block inside `enhanced_filter_with_trend_preservation`; retain finite-value repair and the final `selected[window_size-1:]` contract.

Compute budget: No optimizer. Use at most 12 fixed-frequency components, one weighted least-squares solve per component set, and one optional robust reweighting pass. Expected runtime is below 0.05 seconds for the supplied 1000-sample records.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent spline treats all curvature as an undifferentiated smooth function and therefore either attenuates genuine oscillations or retains noise-induced reversals. Build a deterministic harmonic-plus-drift model
\[
y(t)=a_0+a_1t+a_2t^2+\sum_k(A_k\sin(2\pi f_kt)+B_k\cos(2\pi f_kt)).
\]
Use a fixed logarithmic frequency bank from 0.003 to 0.12 cycles/sample, select no more than 12 frequencies by the reduction in robust residual energy, and fit coefficients with Huber weights based on the MAD residual scale. Include a slowly varying residual component obtained from a three-point integrated random-walk basis, but constrain its second difference by clipping it to two robust residual scales. Reconstruct the entire record, then emit `reconstruction[window_size-1:]`.

This is a mesoscopic replacement rather than an additional smoother: the new representation separates persistent oscillatory energy from broadband noise, while the bounded drift term preserves nonstationary baseline movement. Use QR or `np.linalg.lstsq`, normalize columns before solving, and fall back to the incumbent spline if the design matrix is rank deficient. The output remains finite and has exactly `len(x)-window_size+1` samples.

Expected-gain check: the falsifiable acceptance threshold is a reduction of at least 3 raw output reversals and at least 0.02 in aligned average absolute error relative to the incumbent on the supplied evaluation set; the incumbent spline cannot realize this frequency-selective separation because it has no persistent-frequency state variables.

strategies.title: [state-dependent nonlinear prediction] Echo-state residual denoising
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: deterministic reservoir residual prediction

Replacement scope: Replace only the final `selected` construction in `enhanced_filter_with_trend_preservation`, after `repaired` has been formed. Preserve the existing outlier repair and use the new predictor directly on `repaired`.

Compute budget: One deterministic reservoir start, 80 recurrent units, exactly 8 ridge-regression solves for candidate leak values, and no iterative training. Runtime should remain below 0.1 seconds for a 1000-sample signal.

Gain mechanism: Use a fixed, contractive echo-state reservoir to predict the locally smooth component from the recent signal history while avoiding a free-running unstable forecast. Construct states from the current repaired sample, first difference, and a 12-sample exponentially weighted history. The recurrent matrix is generated deterministically from a fixed trigonometric orthogonal construction, scaled to spectral radius 0.65; the input gain is 0.35. Fit only the linear readout by ridge regression, with the target being the current repaired sample. Blend the reservoir estimate with the repaired sample using a confidence weight
\[
w_t=\frac{\sigma_r^2}{\sigma_r^2+\operatorname{MAD}_{12}(e_t)^2},
\]
where `e` is the one-step residual and `sigma_r` is the global robust residual scale. Limit the correction to 1.5 robust scales per sample, then apply a three-sample monotone slope dead-zone only to corrections smaller than 0.15 scale. This preserves genuine large reversals while removing small recurrent noise reversals.

Unlike a spline or Kalman model, the reservoir supplies nonlinear memory and can represent changing local oscillation shape without requiring an explicit frequency model. Use a short warm-up of 24 samples, copy the repaired samples during warm-up, and emit exactly `selected[window_size-1:]`. If any state or prediction is nonfinite, return `repaired[window_size-1:]`.

Expected-gain check: the falsifiable threshold is at least a 5% reduction in false reversals without increasing aligned recent-window MAE by more than 0.03; the incumbent has no nonlinear memory state and therefore cannot reproduce this bounded history-dependent correction.

strategies.title: [convex total-generalized-variation] Trend-cycle infimal convolution
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: second-order infimal-convolution denoising

Replacement scope: Replace the complete `try` block containing both `UnivariateSpline` calls and candidate selection. Leave the existing nonfinite handling, impulse repair, fallback, and output slicing unchanged.

Compute budget: Two deterministic regularization candidates, each solved by at most 80 primal-dual iterations; no multistart optimizer. Expected runtime is below 0.08 seconds for 1000 samples.

Gain mechanism: Decompose the repaired signal as `x = u + v`, where `u` is a smooth trend with penalized second differences and `v` is an oscillatory detail with penalized first differences:
\[
\min_{u,v}\frac12\|u+v-x\|_2^2+
\lambda_2\|\Delta^2u\|_1+
\lambda_1\|\Delta v\|_1.
\]
Solve this convex infimal-convolution problem with a bounded Chambolle–Pock update and project the dual variables onto their respective L-infinity balls. Use two fixed candidates: a curvature-preserving setting with `(lambda2, lambda1)=(0.9s,0.20s)` and a reversal-suppressing setting `(1.5s,0.35s)`, where `s` is the robust first-difference MAD scale. Select the candidate with lower robust residual plus a penalty of `0.015` per directional reversal. Reconstruct `u+v`, not just `u`, so genuine multi-frequency signal is retained while isolated slope flips are discouraged.

This differs from ordinary spline smoothing because the signal is explicitly split into trend and detail components, and the first- and second-order penalties act on different latent subsystems. Use reflected boundary differences, initialize both components from the repaired signal, and retain the original repaired signal if the solver produces nonfinite values. The emitted result is always exactly `len(x)-window_size+1`.

Expected-gain check: the falsifiable threshold is at least 10% fewer raw slope changes while maintaining correlation above 0.935 and increasing aligned average MAE by less than 0.015; a single cubic spline cannot independently regulate first-order detail and second-order trend curvature.

strategies.plan:

Replacement scope: Replace the complete `try` block in `enhanced_filter_with_trend_preservation`, including the `UnivariateSpline` reconstruction, residual gating, and spline-based candidate selection. Retain the existing finite-value repair and isolated-spike repair before the replacement.

strategies.title: [morphological scale-space] Opening-closing residual impulse suppression
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: morphological scale-space filtering

Replacement scope: Replace only the current three-point `repaired`-signal outlier block. Leave the subsequent spline reconstruction and residual gating unchanged, but feed them a morphology-cleaned signal.

Compute budget: None; perform two vectorized one-dimensional min/max morphology passes with a fixed odd structuring length of `3`, followed by one spline pass already present in the parent. Expected evaluation-time effect is negligible.

Gain mechanism: Construct a lower envelope by erosion followed by dilation and an upper envelope by dilation followed by erosion. Let `opened` and `closed` denote those envelopes, then use the midpoint `(opened + closed)/2` only where the observation lies outside the interval `[opened - 3*sc, closed + 3*sc]`; otherwise preserve the original sample. This is not a median or linear smoother: it removes isolated impulsive excursions while preserving monotone ramps and step plateaus, preventing one bad sample from creating two sign reversals in the downstream derivative. Implement the min/max operations with `scipy.ndimage.minimum_filter1d` and `maximum_filter1d`, using reflected boundaries; if SciPy morphology is unavailable, use the existing repaired array. Preserve the existing exact output slicing.

The falsifiable evaluator check is that, on the fixed evaluation suite, morphology preprocessing must lower `false_reversals` from 14.4 to below 12.5 without increasing `avg_error` above 0.3521; that measurable transformation targets the dominant reversal penalty and would produce a strict combined-score improvement.

strategies.title: [piecewise monotone graph projection] Hysteretic slope-sign reconstruction
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: piecewise monotone graph projection

Replacement scope: Replace the final selected-spline return path after `selected` has been formed. Do not alter spline fitting or residual gating. Apply a bounded slope-sign projection to `selected`, then slice to `window_size-1:`.

Compute budget: None; one linear scan over the reconstructed signal, with no optimizer starts or iterative solver. Expected evaluation-time effect is negligible.

Gain mechanism: Compute a robust derivative scale from `diff(selected)`. Classify each slope as positive, negative, or dead-zone when its magnitude is below `0.35*scale`. Unlike the incumbent’s global reversal-count acceptance test, the projection acts locally and does not discard a useful reconstruction merely because its total reversal count is unchanged.

The falsifiable evaluator check is that the projected output must have fewer than 18 raw slope changes while its aligned correlation remains at least 0.94; those two directly measured conditions target the incumbent’s 22 reversals and preserve its 0.9409 correlation, yielding a strict improvement in the reported combined score.

strategies.title: [robust state-transition graph] Directed slope-transition filtering

strategies.title: [robust multiresolution lifting] Predict-update lifting denoiser
strategies.plan:

The falsifiable threshold is a combined-score improvement to at least `0.755` with output length unchanged; if the evaluator reports less, the multiresolution construction has not exceeded the incumbent.

strategies.title: [rank-envelope morphology] Robust rank-envelope reconstruction
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: rank-envelope morphology

Replacement scope: Replace the current `repaired` construction and the entire spline/residual-gating block inside `enhanced_filter_with_trend_preservation`; retain input sanitization, output slicing, and the Gaussian fallback only for numerical failure.

Compute budget: none; use vectorized NumPy operations with at most three fixed odd-window rank passes, so evaluation time should remain below roughly 2× the incumbent.

Gain mechanism: Construct lower and upper order-statistic envelopes using centered rank filters at radii 1 and 2, then reconstruct the signal by averaging an erosion-dilation opening and dilation-erosion closing. Apply the reconstruction only where the local first-difference sign changes inside the window and the excursion is below `2.5 * MAD(diff)`. Preserve the original sample elsewhere, and finish with a weak three-point convex blend of the reconstructed signal and the original signal. This removes isolated noise-induced extrema without globally suppressing legitimate curvature or introducing spline endpoint excursions. Use reflected padding and crop back to the original length before returning `selected[window_size-1:]`.

The construction is self-contained: for each odd kernel length, compute sliding-window partition ranks with `numpy.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view`; define erosion and dilation as the minimum and maximum of each window, opening as dilation after erosion, and closing as erosion after dilation. Estimate the local noise scale from the global MAD of first differences, with a positive floor. Preserve the exact required output length and retain the incumbent spline result as a finite-value fallback only.

Expected-gain check: the incumbent has 22 slope changes and 14.4 false reversals; this replacement is accepted as a genuine improvement only if evaluation reports at least 10% fewer slope changes and false reversals while keeping average error below 0.37, a directly falsifiable condition that targets the two dominant reversal penalties.

strategies.title: [phase-manifold projection] Bounded phase-space curvature projection
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: phase-manifold projection

Replacement scope: Replace only the final `selected` generation after `rz` is available; retain the incumbent robust spline and residual-gating stages as the provisional estimate.

Compute budget: none; one deterministic projection pass over the signal, using vectorized lagged arrays and at most two scalar clipping passes. Expected runtime increase is negligible.

Gain mechanism: Represent the provisional estimate with the lag-1 state pair `(y[t-1], y[t])` and estimate a robust local velocity and acceleration envelope from the middle 60% of finite second differences. Project only anomalous state transitions onto a bounded-curvature continuation:
`v[t] = clip(y[t]-y[t-1], median(v) ± 3*MAD(v))`,
then `a[t] = clip(v[t]-v[t-1], ±2.5*MAD(a))`.
Reconstruct the projected sequence by integrating the clipped velocity, but blend it with the original provisional estimate using a weight proportional to the excess curvature. Do not clip ordinary slopes; only transitions whose curvature exceeds the robust envelope are altered. This changes the representation from pointwise residual gating to a phase-space invariant and specifically suppresses alternating slope reversals that the incumbent can retain even when pointwise residuals are small.

Use the provisional `rz` when finite, otherwise `z`; preserve its first two samples exactly, integrate from the second sample, and apply a bounded correction no larger than 35% of the local robust velocity. Return the aligned suffix with no change to the public interface or output length.

Expected-gain check: because the incumbent’s reversal count is 22, the projection has a measurable target of reducing reversals to 18 or fewer without increasing the aligned average error above 0.37; failure to meet either threshold rejects the mechanism.

strategies.title: [adaptive quantile-state] Two-sided quantile state smoother
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: adaptive quantile-state smoothing

Replacement scope: Replace the complete `try` block containing both `UnivariateSpline` fits and residual winsorization; keep the existing repaired signal, exception handling, and suffix slicing.

Compute budget: none; two forward/backward scalar recursions and one vectorized residual-scale calculation. Runtime should be linear in signal length and materially below the existing spline cost.

Gain mechanism: Estimate a forward robust state using an asymmetric quantile update and estimate a backward state on the reversed signal. At each sample, update the state with a clipped innovation:
`q = clip(x[t]-state, -k*s[t], k*s[t])`,
where `s[t]` is an exponentially updated absolute-innovation scale and `k=2.2`. Use a larger gain when the innovation persists with the same sign for two consecutive samples and a smaller gain for isolated sign changes. Average the forward and backward states to remove phase bias. This is not a fixed low-pass filter: persistent directional motion is tracked quickly, while isolated innovations and alternating reversals are attenuated. Estimate scale with a robust initial MAD and a bounded exponential update, and use reflection-equivalent initialization from the first three repaired samples.

Return the bidirectional state estimate directly, selecting it over the incumbent only when it is finite and its residual MAD is no greater than 1.08 times the repaired-signal residual MAD. This preserves a safe incumbent fallback while providing a distinct adaptive quantile-state mechanism. The output remains exactly `n-window_size+1`.

Expected-gain check: the new persistent-sign gain must reduce the recent-window lag error below 0.30 while keeping total reversal count at or below 22; these are explicit evaluator thresholds for the responsiveness/smoothness tradeoff that the incumbent does not control directly.

strategies.title: [second-difference-penalized reconstruction] Hodrick–Prescott batch smoother
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: second-difference-penalized reconstruction

Replacement scope: Replace the entire `try` block inside `enhanced_filter_with_trend_preservation`, including both `UnivariateSpline` fits and the reversal-based selection. Preserve the existing finite-value repair and isolated-spike repair before the replacement.

Compute budget: No optimizer starts and no iterative optimizer. Solve one symmetric positive-definite banded linear system of size `n`; use `scipy.linalg.solve_banded` when SciPy is available, with a dense `numpy.linalg.solve` fallback. The expected evaluation-time increase is negligible for the supplied signal lengths.

Gain mechanism: Minimize
`sum_i (x_i - z_i)^2 + lambda * sum_i (z[i+2] - 2*z[i+1] + z[i])^2`
with a deterministic `lambda = clip(0.30 * n * sc**2, 1e-4, 25*n)`, where `sc` is the already-computed robust difference scale. Unlike the incumbent cubic spline, this directly penalizes curvature through a fixed second-difference operator, does not introduce spline-knot behavior or residual refitting, and produces a globally coupled trend with substantially fewer small slope reversals. Use natural second-difference boundary rows, retain the repaired observations in the data term, and return `z[window_size-1:]`. The fixed linear system always returns exactly `n-window_size+1` finite values, so the public validity contract is preserved.

Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom is direct curvature regularization rather than spline residual gating; it should be accepted only if the evaluator reports at least 10% fewer raw slope changes than 22 while keeping average error below 0.40, a falsifiable condition implying improvement in the dominant reversal terms without requiring an unavailable clean signal.

strategies.title: [rank-preserving order-statistics] Hampel plateau-and-edge repair
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: rank-preserving order-statistics reconstruction

Replacement scope: Replace only the current three-point `repaired` spike-repair block. Leave the subsequent smoothing stage unchanged, but feed it a robustly repaired signal.

Compute budget: No optimizer and no iterative solver. Perform two vectorized rolling-median passes using `scipy.ndimage.median_filter` with kernel sizes 3 and 5, plus one vectorized local MAD estimate. Expected evaluation-time effect is below a few milliseconds for the supplied records.

Gain mechanism: The current repair detects only an isolated point using its two immediate neighbors, so two- or three-sample noise bursts survive and generate several counted reversals. Compute a radius-2 rolling median `m5`, local MAD `mad5 = median_filter(abs(x-m5), 5)`, and replace a sample only when `abs(x-m5) > 3.0*max(1.4826*mad5, sc)`. Then apply a conservative radius-1 replacement for remaining impulses using the radius-3 median. This is an order-statistics outlier detector rather than a smoother: genuine broad extrema survive because they are supported across the window, while unsupported sign-flipping excursions are removed before the incumbent reconstruction. Preserve the original endpoints and return the incumbent’s exact slice.

Expected-gain check: The new mechanism can remove multi-sample bursts that the incumbent’s two-neighbor test cannot represent; the falsifiable acceptance threshold is a reduction of false reversals from 14.4 to at most 12.5 with correlation no lower than 0.935, which directly targets the incumbent’s largest unaddressed reversal penalty.

strategies.title: [shape-preserving polynomial projection] Savitzky–Golay curvature-limited recons
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: shape-preserving polynomial projection

Replacement scope: Replace `enhanced_filter_with_trend_preservation` completely, while retaining its signature and finite-input handling. Do not call the spline, Gaussian fallback, or reversal-count selector.

Compute budget: Evaluate at most three fixed candidates, with no optimizer starts and no iterations: Savitzky–Golay filters with `(window, polynomial order)` equal to `(9, 2)`, `(13, 3)`, and `(17, 3)`. Select deterministically using a robust observable score
`0.55 * reversal_count + 0.45 * sum(abs(second_difference)) / max(sc, 1e-7)`,
subject to each candidate’s residual MAD being no more than 1.35 times the input residual MAD. Expected runtime is small because each candidate is a compiled convolution/filter operation.

Gain mechanism: Replace the incumbent’s global spline with local polynomial projection, which preserves turning-point curvature and sinusoidal amplitude better than a broad low-pass while still suppressing alternating noise. The candidate score explicitly balances reversal suppression against curvature loss; the residual constraint prevents choosing a flat candidate solely because it has fewer reversals. Use odd windows no larger than 17, pad by reflection, and slice only after filtering so the evaluator’s fixed index alignment is preserved. If SciPy is unavailable, use the original incumbent implementation as a fallback; every normal path returns exactly `n-window_size+1` finite samples.

Expected-gain check: The new selectable polynomial basis can reduce lag and amplitude distortion that the incumbent spline introduces; the falsifiable threshold is average aligned absolute error below 0.34 while raw slope changes remain no greater than 22, which would improve the two lag terms without sacrificing the incumbent’s smoothness baseline.

strategies.title: [robust total-variation trend filtering] Huber-TV with curvature continuation
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: robust Huber total-variation trend filtering

Replacement scope: Replace the entire `UnivariateSpline`/residual-gating block inside `enhanced_filter_with_trend_preservation`, retaining the existing finite-value repair and the final `selected[window_size-1:]` contract.

Compute budget: None; use a deterministic banded primal-dual or ADMM solver with at most 80 iterations and one initialization. Runtime should remain below roughly 0.05 seconds for the default 1000-sample input.

Gain mechanism: Optimize
`sum(rho(y[i]-x[i])) + lambda1*sum(rho(d1[y])) + lambda2*sum(d2[y]**2)`
where `rho` is Huber loss, `lambda1` is selected from `0.10*sc` to `0.35*sc`, and `lambda2=0.015`. Use continuation from `lambda1=0.35*sc` to the selected value, warm-starting each stage. The first-difference Huber term removes small slope sign changes without forcing genuine large reversals to zero, while the second-difference penalty prevents staircase artifacts. Unlike the incumbent's spline residual gate, this directly penalizes reversal-producing increments and remains robust to isolated impulses.
